question:
Deutchlander Machine Company (DMC) manufactures two types of printing presses: a four-color litho and a two-color litho. Demand for both products is high and exceeds DMC's production capacity. The production is constrained by the availability of steel rollers, gear cutting capacity, and roller polishing capacity. The following Table details the requirements for each type of press. DMC can acquire 100 steel rollers per week, has 160 hours available for gear cutting, and 40 hours for roller polishing each week. To maintain market presence without increasing prices, DMC aims to produce at least two units of each press weekly. The profit for each four-color press is DM24,000 and for each two-color press is DM10,000. Maximize DMC's profit.

Table (Resource requirements for each type of printing press):
| Printing Press Type | Steel Rollers Required | Gear Cutting Time (hours) | Polishing Time (hours) | Profit per Unit (DM) |
| ------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| Four-color litho    | 16                     | 30                        | 8                      | 24,000               |
| Two-color litho     | 8                      | 12                        | 3                      | 10,000               |

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "products": ["four_color", "two_color"],
    "resources": ["steel_rollers", "gear_cutting", "polishing"],
    "profit": {"four_color": 24000, "two_color": 10000},
    # usage[resource][product]
    "usage": {
        "steel_rollers": {"four_color": 16, "two_color": 8},
        "gear_cutting": {"four_color": 30, "two_color": 12},
        "polishing": {"four_color": 8, "two_color": 3},
    },
    "availability": {
        "steel_rollers": 100,
        "gear_cutting": 160,
        "polishing": 40,
    },
    "min_production": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    m.R = pyo.Set(initialize=d["resources"])

    # Variables: weekly production quantity per press type (integer units)
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: maximize total weekly profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["profit"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P)

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # Resource capacity constraints
    def capacity_rule(m, r):
        return sum(d["usage"][r][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.P) <= d["availability"][r]

    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.R, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Minimum production requirement for each press type
    def min_prod_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= d["min_production"]

    m.min_production = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=min_prod_rule)

    return m

def build_model(data=None):

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of product types
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=["four", "two"])

    # Decision variables: number of presses of each type (integer units)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Resource constraint definitions
    def rollers_rule(m):
        # 16*x_four + 8*x_two <= 100
        return (d["steel_rollers"]["four"] * m.x["four"]
                + d["steel_rollers"]["two"] * m.x["two"]
                <= d["avail_rollers"])

    def gear_rule(m):
        # 30*x_four + 12*x_two <= 160
        return (d["gear_cutting"]["four"] * m.x["four"]
                + d["gear_cutting"]["two"] * m.x["two"]
                <= d["avail_gear"])

    def polish_rule(m):
        # 8*x_four + 3*x_two <= 40
        return (d["polishing"]["four"] * m.x["four"]
                + d["polishing"]["two"] * m.x["two"]
                <= d["avail_polish"])

    model.con_rollers = pyo.Constraint(rule=rollers_rule)
    model.con_gear = pyo.Constraint(rule=gear_rule)
    model.con_polish = pyo.Constraint(rule=polish_rule)

    # Minimum production of at least two units of each press (>= 2)
    def min_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= d["min_each"]

    model.con_min = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=min_rule)

    # Objective: maximize total profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (d["profit"]["four"] * m.x["four"]
                + d["profit"]["two"] * m.x["two"])

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   x[p] : number of presses of type p produced per week
#          p in PRESS_TYPES = {"four_color", "two_color"}
#          domain: NonNegativeIntegers (units are indivisible)
#          lower bound: at least 2 units of each press type per week
#
# Objective (maximize):
#   Total weekly profit = 24000 * x[four_color] + 10000 * x[two_color]
#
# Constraints:
#   (1) Steel rollers:  16*x[four_color] + 8*x[two_color]  <= 100   (rollers/week)
#   (2) Gear cutting:   30*x[four_color] + 12*x[two_color] <= 160   (hours/week)
#   (3) Polishing:       8*x[four_color] +  3*x[two_color] <=  40   (hours/week)
#   (4) Minimum demand: x[p] >= 2 for each press type p
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "PRESS_TYPES": ["four_color", "two_color"],

    # Profit per unit (DM)
    "PROFIT": {
        "four_color": 24000,
        "two_color": 10000,
    },

    # Resource usage per unit of each press type
    "STEEL_ROLLERS": {
        "four_color": 16,
        "two_color": 8,
    },
    "GEAR_HOURS": {
        "four_color": 30,
        "two_color": 12,
    },
    "POLISH_HOURS": {
        "four_color": 8,
        "two_color": 3,
    },

    # Resource availability per week
    "STEEL_ROLLERS_AVAIL": 100,
    "GEAR_HOURS_AVAIL": 160,
    "POLISH_HOURS_AVAIL": 40,

    # Minimum production of each press type per week
    "MIN_UNITS": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of press types
    model.PRESS_TYPES = pyo.Set(initialize=d["PRESS_TYPES"])

    # Decision variables: integer units produced, at least MIN_UNITS each
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.PRESS_TYPES,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(d["MIN_UNITS"], None),
    )

    # Objective: maximize total weekly profit
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["PROFIT"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.PRESS_TYPES)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # (1) Steel rollers availability
    def steel_rule(m):
        return sum(d["STEEL_ROLLERS"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.PRESS_TYPES) \
            <= d["STEEL_ROLLERS_AVAIL"]

    model.steel_rollers = pyo.Constraint(rule=steel_rule)

    # (2) Gear cutting capacity
    def gear_rule(m):
        return sum(d["GEAR_HOURS"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.PRESS_TYPES) \
            <= d["GEAR_HOURS_AVAIL"]

    model.gear_cutting = pyo.Constraint(rule=gear_rule)

    # (3) Roller polishing capacity
    def polish_rule(m):
        return sum(d["POLISH_HOURS"][p] * m.x[p] for p in m.PRESS_TYPES) \
            <= d["POLISH_HOURS_AVAIL"]

    model.polishing = pyo.Constraint(rule=polish_rule)

    # (4) Minimum production of each press type
    def min_units_rule(m, p):
        return m.x[p] >= d["MIN_UNITS"]

    model.min_units = pyo.Constraint(model.PRESS_TYPES, rule=min_units_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Decision variables
#   x4 : number of four-color litho presses produced per week
#        (index set: none; domain: NonNegativeIntegers, lower bound 2)
#   x2 : number of two-color litho presses produced per week
#        (index set: none; domain: NonNegativeIntegers, lower bound 2)
#
# Objective (maximize): total weekly profit
#   max  24000 * x4 + 10000 * x2
#
# Constraints
#   (1) Steel rollers: 16*x4 + 8*x2 <= 100          [100 rollers/week available]
#   (2) Gear cutting:  30*x4 + 12*x2 <= 160         [160 hours/week available]
#   (3) Polishing:      8*x4 + 3*x2 <= 40           [40 hours/week available]
#   (4) Market presence: x4 >= 2 and x2 >= 2        [at least two of each press]
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DATA = {
    "profit_four": 24000,      # DM per four-color press
    "profit_two": 10000,       # DM per two-color press
    "rollers_four": 16,        # steel rollers per four-color press
    "rollers_two": 8,          # steel rollers per two-color press
    "rollers_avail": 100,      # steel rollers available per week
    "gear_four": 30,           # gear cutting hours per four-color press
    "gear_two": 12,            # gear cutting hours per two-color press
    "gear_avail": 160,         # gear cutting hours available per week
    "polish_four": 8,          # polishing hours per four-color press
    "polish_two": 3,           # polishing hours per two-color press
    "polish_avail": 40,        # polishing hours available per week
    "min_four": 2,             # minimum four-color presses per week
    "min_two": 2,              # minimum two-color presses per week
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Decision variables
    model.x4 = pyo.Var(
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(d["min_four"], None),
    )
    model.x2 = pyo.Var(
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(d["min_two"], None),
    )

    # Objective: maximize total weekly profit
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=d["profit_four"] * model.x4 + d["profit_two"] * model.x2,
        sense=pyo.maximize,
    )

    # (1) Steel rollers availability
    model.steel_rollers = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=d["rollers_four"] * model.x4 + d["rollers_two"] * model.x2
        <= d["rollers_avail"]
    )

    # (2) Gear cutting capacity
    model.gear_cutting = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=d["gear_four"] * model.x4 + d["gear_two"] * model.x2
        <= d["gear_avail"]
    )

    # (3) Roller polishing capacity
    model.polishing = pyo.Constraint(
        expr=d["polish_four"] * model.x4 + d["polish_two"] * model.x2
        <= d["polish_avail"]
    )

    # (4) Minimum production for market presence is enforced via variable bounds.

    return model
